newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical says Q3 felt price erosion.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical says Q3 felt price erosion.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said it experienced price erosion of $433 million and a $100 million increase in feedstock and energy costs in the third quarter.
Quarterly sales $5 billion were up two percent from the same period a year ago, reflecting the nine percent decline in prices and an 11 percent volume increase, Dow said.
The chemicals giant said operating income was down $200 million to $746 million, versus $946 million a year ago. Dow said it cut expenses by five percent in the third quarter.
The chemicals and metals segment reported operating income of $203 million versus $324 million a year ago, Dow said.

Higher energy costs and lower prices for caustic soda and vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) compared to a year ago contributed to this segment's declines in revenue and earnings. Prices for VCM, however, have trended upward from the second quarter of this year.

Dow said its Performance Chemicals posted operating income of $100 million, up 11 percent from $90 million in the third quarter of 1995. Specialty Chemicals recorded higher year-over-year profits for the eleventh consecutive quarter, a result of volume growth and the strategic portfolio restructuring undertaken by that business.
